investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-21T10:05–10:13Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the other 4 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is unconfirmed.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously, scheduling always fails.
Cluster under-provisioning for remote-agent workloads: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, which may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workloads.

Peer-pod provider quota or VM pool exhaustion at the infrastructure layer beneath Kubernetes: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource count is derived from an external VM pool; if that pool is exhausted or the provider is rate-limiting, the extended resource count drops to zero.
Node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec are overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run the workload if the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were present on them.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-21T10:08–10:13Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 of those nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) is exhausted of the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 125–151 seconds, preventing agent creation and causing all three remote-agents checks to fail before any API evidence could be collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. If the affinity rule is overly restrictive or a node label was removed, the effective capacity is permanently reduced.

TERTIARY — Transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads (from users, other evals, or background jobs) temporarily consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, causing a time-bounded capacity exhaustion that may self-resolve once existing pods terminate.

QUATERNARY — Node pool under-provisioning or autoscaler lag: the cluster may lack autoscaling for kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, or the autoscaler did not trigger in time to satisfy the eval pod within the scheduling window.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no response evidence — leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 125–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity would appear to drop even if total VM slots are unchanged.

Tertiary — VM pool not scaled to meet concurrent eval demand: the eval suite submits multiple remote-agent pods in sequence (create → state → runtime), and if prior eval runs left leaked VMs occupying slots, the pool may be perpetually exhausted. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) but a prior cleanup failure could leave orphaned VMs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node maintenance, eviction storm, or scale-down): a temporary reduction in ready nodes could produce the same symptom without a persistent capacity problem. No history data is available (previousRunCount=0) to distinguish transient from persistent.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-21T10:05–10:13Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM never started.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node cluster because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the other 4 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact is unconfirmed.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible. If those 2 nodes lose capacity simultaneously, scheduling always fails.
Cluster under-provisioning for remote-agent workloads: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, which may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workloads.

Peer-pod provider quota or VM pool exhaustion at the infrastructure layer beneath Kubernetes: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource count is derived from an external VM pool; if that pool is exhausted or the provider is rate-limiting, the extended resource count drops to zero.
Node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec are overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise run the workload if the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were present on them.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no response evidence — leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 125–146 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which must provision a remote VM pod — this is the call that triggers the failing Kubernetes scheduling path.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new eval pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity would appear to drop even if total VM slots are unchanged.

Tertiary — VM pool not scaled to meet concurrent eval demand: the eval suite submits multiple remote-agent pods in sequence (create → state → runtime), and if prior eval runs left leaked VMs occupying slots, the pool may be perpetually exhausted. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) but a prior cleanup failure could leave orphaned VMs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node maintenance, eviction storm, or scale-down): a temporary reduction in ready nodes could produce the same symptom without a persistent capacity problem. No history data is available (previousRunCount=0) to distinguish transient from persistent.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: Confirms that create, state, and runtime all fail with the same Unschedulable message, ruling out a runtime-only regression.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the two affinity-matching nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (e.g., kubectl describe node) to check the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on the nodes that match the pod's affinity selector. No specific command is supplied because no kubectl context or cluster name appears in the evidence.

reproductionSteps.label: List running remote-agent pods to check for leaked or long-running VMs consuming VM slots
reproductionSteps.details: Query the namespace where remote-agent pods are scheduled to identify any pods that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs or user sessions. No specific namespace or cluster name appears in the evidence.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes VM scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool)
affectedAreas.reason: All three eval checks report the identical Unschedulable scheduler message citing Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity selector (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all VM capacity onto 2 nodes and amplifying any resource pressure (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — eval checks: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) are failing. remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true, meaning the feature is in a degraded/outage state per the registry thresholds (degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the Kubernetes pod scheduling path that is failing. The withCleanup wrapper at line 1916 is also implicated if prior cleanup failures left orphaned VM pods.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on the two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity selector to confirm whether the pool is exhausted.
Audit running and pending remote-agent pods in the production namespace for leaked VMs that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs or user sessions; terminate any orphaned pods to free VM slots.
If the VM pool is confirmed exhausted by legitimate workloads, scale up the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool or increase the VM slot quota on existing nodes to restore scheduling headroom.

Review the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods to determine whether 4 of 6 nodes being excluded is intentional; if not, correct the selector to distribute scheduling pressure across more nodes.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true in features.json (lines 183–184) and both are failing, treat the remote-agents feature as degraded per the registry threshold (degradedAfterFailures=1) until scheduling is restored and the evals pass.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or was transient at the time of the original run. A pass on re-run suggests a transient cluster event; a repeat fail confirms ongoing capacity exhaustion.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that the shared Unschedulable failure pattern persists across all three checks, confirming a cluster-level cause rather than a check-specific regression.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on affinity-matching nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the resource-exhaustion hypothesis by showing current allocatable vs. in-use VM slot counts on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity selector.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all running and pending remote-agent pods in the production namespace
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked or long-running pods from prior eval runs or user sessions are occupying VM slots, which would explain persistent exhaustion even after eval cleanup.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not exhausted, the resource-exhaustion hypothesis is disproved and the cause is likely a scheduler policy or affinity misconfiguration.
If the eval passes on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief node maintenance window) rather than a persistent capacity problem.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime path rather than the shared VM scheduling layer.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type exists on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node label or resource registration rather than exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude more nodes, and the two remaining nodes have sufficient VM capacity, the cause would be affinity misconfiguration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-matching nodes and alerts before the pool reaches 100% utilization, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that counts running remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if leaked pods are detected, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust the pool.

Add a node affinity/selector validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod selector, alerting if the count drops below a minimum threshold (e.g., below 3 nodes).

Add a historical baseline to the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks so that currentlyRegressedFromPass can be populated on future runs, enabling regression detection against a known-good state.
